headline: High-risk data exfiltration and compliance exposure: dexter’s broad egress can move financial data while pathway has no egress or file access, limiting direct pairwise conflict but not downstream leakage.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented: dexter has broad network egress and scratchpad files, while pathway has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem read/write, or MCP surfaces. Without a bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is introduced between dexter and pathway, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not connect dexter scratchpad files to pathway inputs.
Disable any future clipboard or queue bridge between them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API calls, so sensitive context can leave the local environment. Pathway has no network egress and no file access, which reduces direct leakage from B, but the pair still creates a one-way exfiltration path through A’s outbound APIs.
conditions: IF dexter is given financial records or secrets in its scratchpad, outbound API calls can transmit them.
IF pathway is later granted file or network access, the leakage surface expands.
mitigations: Restrict dexter inputs to non-sensitive samples.
Remove secrets from dexter’s environment before running.
Route dexter through a redaction proxy.
Keep pathway offline and file-isolated.
Review outbound API destinations before execution.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and autonomous execution, but pathway cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct write-write conflict is unlikely unless new shared state is added.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent.
Avoid shared git repositories.
Serialize any future writes through one coordinator.
Keep pathway read-only.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter can generate autonomous outputs from APIs and scratchpad files, and pathway is a document-processing agent that could consume those outputs as inputs. The profiles do not show verification or provenance checks, so if pathway treats dexter’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream documents or actions.
conditions: IF pathway ingests dexter-generated text without validation, cascading errors are possible.
IF dexter’s outputs are used as source-of-truth for downstream documents, the blast radius grows.
mitigations: Add a human review step for dexter outputs.
Require provenance tags on all dexter-generated content.
Compare outputs against a second source before use.
Limit pathway to draft-only processing.
Reject unverified facts from dexter.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and requests multiple API keys, while pathway’s residency, retention, and certification posture are undocumented. Because dexter has broad egress, sensitive financial data could flow to external services without a documented compliance boundary; uncertainty here escalates severity.
conditions: IF dexter processes regulated financial records, external API transmission may create a compliance breach.
IF pathway is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter residency or retention rules, the mismatch becomes more severe.
mitigations: Classify all dexter inputs before execution.
Block regulated records from outbound APIs.
Document retention and deletion rules for both agents.
Run a compliance review on all third-party endpoints.
Use synthetic data for testing.
